_comment: Security baseline of the development image 0.0.61 (ports as proto:scope:port, LLMNR off and no sudo/pkexec/pam_timestamp_check setuid since RUY-18), checked by scripts/vm-security-check.sh (T-424). Measured with 'vm-security-check.sh measure' on a booted image. A looser value needs a reason in the same commit.

ruya-boot-marker.service.reason: root oneshot, measured 0.0.61 - barely hardened, should not ship, to be tightened (Inbox, T-425)

ruya-compositor@.service.reason: needs DRM, input and the GPU, measured 0.0.61 - barely hardened, should not ship, to be tightened (Inbox, T-425)

ruya-flathub-remote.service.reason: root oneshot with network, measured 0.0.61 - barely hardened, should not ship, to be tightened (Inbox, T-425)

ruya-grub-menu.service.reason: root oneshot that writes the GRUB custom.cfg on /boot; measured 0.0.61

ruya-inputd.service.reason: own user ruya-input, no caps, no IP; reads /dev/input, uinput; no PrivateNetwork (the udev monitor, 06-input.md section 3); measured 0.0.69-input (RUY-3)

ruya-library.service.reason: own user, no caps, no network; measured 0.0.61

ruya-notifications.service.reason: root (owns its bus name), empty capability set, no network, writes only its StateDirectory; the ruya-session.service hardening (1.1). Not measured yet: RUY-730 set it on the host, the first VM run of vm-notifications-check.sh measures it

ruya-session.service.reason: root, empty capability set, no network, 01-platform.md section 3 (T-162); measured 0.0.61

ruya-platform.service.reason: root (owns its bus name), empty capability set and ProtectProc=invisible (ADR-022 decision 4: the identity helper reads a caller's .flatpak-info), no network, writes only its StateDirectory; the ruya-notifications hardening. Measured 1.1 on the Dell (0.0.106 with the RUY-1129 units and binaries, transient)

ruya-platform-identify@.service.reason: root, socket-activated per request of ruya-platform only (0600 root socket), exactly CAP_SYS_PTRACE and CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH (another uid's /proc/<pid>/root/.flatpak-info, 0600), no bus (InaccessiblePaths=/run/dbus), no network, no address family, one task, 5 s; ADR-022 decision 4. Measured 1.6 on the Dell (0.0.106 with the RUY-1129 units, transient)

ruya-play.service.reason: estimate (RUY-829), not measured yet: root with CAP_CHOWN/DAC/FOWNER for the Flatpak commit and network for a missing runtime, hardened as ruya-store (3.3); RUY-100 measures it

public_bus_doors._comment: The only bus names whose policy may allow anything in the default context (ADR-022: a sandboxed app's one door), and the interfaces it may open there: send (method_call) to them and receive their signals, nothing else. Every listed interface must have every element tagged org.ruyaos.Stability in api/dbus/<name>.xml. Read by scripts/lint-bus-policies.ps1 (host) and vm-security-check.sh busrecv (the policy as installed).

service_signals.reason: Library1.Rescan asks root ruya-session for a profile's Steam scan (ADR-045 amendment, owner 2026-11-25). dbus-broker checks a broadcast's send rules against each receiver's names, so without this allow Session1's default deny drops the signal. The only signal a service user may send to another service; read by scripts/lint-bus-policies.ps1 (rule 2).

private_state.reason: The PIN hashes never leave ruya-profiles (RUY-1130, ADR-022 decision 4): root reads any file whatever its mode, so the store has its own 0700 directory and every other ruya-* unit that runs as root (or holds a reading capability) hides it, and /sysroot (on bootc /var is a bind of /sysroot/ostree/deploy/<stateroot>/var, so the same directory is there too), with InaccessiblePaths=, and a unit with CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH keeps open_by_handle_at out of its SystemCallFilter allow list; ruya-profiles is not dumpable, so its own /proc/<pid>/root is closed to every peer without CAP_SYS_PTRACE (and it writes no core dump). The hiding is one layer, not the boundary: ruya-profiles' children (useradd, userdel, loginctl, getent; src/accounts.rs) are dumpable again after execve, so while one runs a root peer with a capability superset (ruya-play, ruya-store) can read the store through /proc/<child>/root, until ADR-049 (ruya-profiles as its own user, a bus-less root accounts helper). A directory, not the file: the store's tmp + rename would undo a hidden file. Read by scripts/lint-private-state.ps1 (host) and vm-profiles-check.sh private (the running units).

exceptions.reason: bootc needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN (it remounts /sysroot writable in its own mount namespace and writes the deployment there, so /sysroot cannot be hidden) and CAP_SYS_PTRACE (it reads /proc/1/ns/mnt): either undoes a hide. It reads the store like any root process with those capabilities; RUY-1130 does not change it.

Its job is CAP_SYS_PTRACE + CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH (another uid's /proc/<pid>/root/.flatpak-info, ADR-022 decision 4, RUY-1129), which also opens a non-dumpable ruya-profiles' /proc/<pid>/root. Socket-activated by ruya-platform only, one task, no bus, no network, 5 s, reads only a file the request's uid owns.
Root oneshot with CAP_SYS_ADMIN and @mount to remount /boot writable for its copy: it could unmount the cover. Runs once at boot, no network, writes only /boot/grub2/custom.cfg.

xwayland_domains.reason: RUY-436 (ADR-034): the X server of an X11-only app, started on demand by the app's helper as the profile user. Fedora's policy labels /usr/bin/Xwayland xserver_t (seen on the Dell spike, RUY-1); the image adds no module for it. RUY-20 (SELinux domains for the ruya-* services) does not cover it: Xwayland is not a ruya-* process. Confirm on the first VM run of vm-x11-check.sh.
